skill.name: playwright-browser-automation
skill.description: Run Playwright browser automation for web testing. It detects local development servers, writes temporary scripts, opens a visible browser, fills forms, checks links, captures screenshots, and tests responsive layouts.
skill.summary: Automate browser checks with Playwright scripts, screenshots, and local dev server detection.
skill.author: Claude Assistant

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in SKILL.md, helpers.js, and prisma/schema.prisma are false positives from Markdown backticks, example localhost URLs, or schema tokens. The real risks are the run.js arbitrary JavaScript execution workflow, automatic install commands, disabled browser sandbox flags, and localhost service probing.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before execution, run scripts in a sandboxed process, and restrict inputs to reviewed Playwright templates when possible.
Remove --no-sandbox and --disable-setuid-sandbox by default, and document the rare container cases where users may opt in.
Move npm install and browser installation to an explicit setup step with pinned dependencies and clear user consent.

remediation.issue: Localhost port probing for server detection
remediation.suggestion: Ask for consent before probing ports, allow a user-supplied port list, and report exactly which local ports are checked.

remediation.issue: Unrelated Prisma schema included with the skill
remediation.suggestion: Remove prisma/schema.prisma unless it is required for the skill, to reduce audit noise around credentials, webhooks, and screenshots.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks miss defects across viewports, forms, and login flows. This skill uses Playwright scripts to run visible browser tests, capture screenshots, and report results from local or supplied URLs.
actual_capabilities: Detects common local development server ports before running localhost tests.
Creates and runs Playwright scripts for page checks, login flows, forms, and link validation.
Captures full-page and viewport screenshots for desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.
Provides helper functions for safe clicks, text entry, cookie banners, table extraction, and retries.
Runs browser automation from a file, inline script, or standard input through a local executor.
limitations: It requires Node.js, Playwright, and a browser runtime on the local machine.
It executes local JavaScript through run.js, so untrusted automation requests require sandboxing and review.
It does not include a persistent test runner, assertion framework, or CI configuration by itself.
It mainly targets browser workflows and does not validate server-side behavior directly.

use_cases.title: Check a Local Web App
use_cases.description: Detect a running local server, open the page, capture screenshots, and report visible page issues.

use_cases.title: Validate User Flows
use_cases.description: Exercise login, form submission, navigation, and redirect behavior with custom Playwright steps.

use_cases.title: Review Responsive Layouts
use_cases.description: Test pages across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewport sizes and compare screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Page Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Playwright browser automation skill to find my local dev server, open the home page, and save a full-page screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to test the contact form on my local app. Fill sample values, submit it, and report whether a success message appears.

prompt_templates.title: Check Responsive Views
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a responsive review for the dashboard page at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths. Capture screenshots and list layout problems.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complete Login Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Automate the login journey with provided test credentials, verify the dashboard redirect, inspect key elements, and summarize failures with screenshots.

output_examples.input: Test whether my local marketing page renders correctly.
output_examples.output: Detected one local server, opened the marketing page, captured a screenshot, and reported the page title and visible layout issues.

output_examples.input: Check the login flow and confirm the redirect.
output_examples.output: Filled the login form with test credentials, submitted it, observed the dashboard redirect, and noted any selector or timeout failures.

output_examples.input: Review the page on mobile and desktop.
output: Captured desktop, tablet, and mobile screenshots.
Compared visible navigation, content fit, and form usability.
Reported responsive issues with viewport context.

best_practices: Run browser automation only against URLs you own or have permission to test.
Use dedicated test accounts and avoid real credentials in prompts or scripts.
Review generated scripts before execution when testing sensitive apps or authenticated flows.
anti_patterns: Do not run unreviewed automation from unknown users against private applications.
Do not store production passwords or API keys in generated test scripts.
Do not use visible browser automation as the only validation for critical backend logic.

faq.question: Does this skill require Playwright to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects Node.js and Playwright dependencies. The included runner can install Playwright when dependencies are missing.

faq.question: Can it test local development servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It probes common localhost ports and asks for a choice when multiple servers are found.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated flows?
faq.answer: Yes. Use dedicated test credentials and avoid production accounts or secrets.

faq.question: Does it create permanent test files?
faq.answer: No. The workflow writes temporary scripts and screenshots, commonly under /tmp, unless the user requests another location.

faq.question: Is it safe to run against any website?
faq.answer: No. Run it only on sites you own or have permission to test, and avoid untrusted scripts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
